about: Things the playtester has said they like (keep) or dislike (avoid), in their words, with the settings behind them. test/pins.test.ts fails if a pinned value moves: that is the cue to ask before changing it, then update the pin with the new quote.

keep.said: Strafing, turning didn't feel like I was actually turning, whereas the original movement did
the size of the kaiju I had above was feeling better
Let's play around with some options (drunk style, more normal movement rules, even something faster paced with slides, jumps)
we still want that Hard to Control but Fun feel
Sneeze meter needs to fill up faster (then: no complaint about the faster one)

avoid.said: The skill check on carrying is still too distracting - by trying to focus on the circle, it's hard to see where to go
avoid.means: Nothing that needs watching away from the kaiju while carrying. Prompts sit at the side and say one thing.

avoid.said: Having to hold with E makes it tough to walk
avoid.means: No held buttons for carrying: click to take hold, click to let go.

avoid.said: the settings were a lot, and hard to really see how they worked together
avoid.means: The panel opens on the six feel dials. New knobs go under Advanced.

avoid.said: movement is OK, but not fun. It feels very sluggish
avoid.means: Weight comes from animation, camera and feedback, never from making the kaiju slow to answer. The default style must be properly moving within about half a second of the key.

avoid.said: get rid of the hat, and the vest. We're a monster. Well natured, but not like a kids show. Try to make the kaiju look a little more realistic, less goofy
avoid.means: No costumes, no googly eyes, no cartoon props on the kaiju. Good-natured comes from how it moves and reacts.

avoid.said: The city is also maybe a little too narrow streets (or the kaiju needs to be a little smaller)
avoid.means: A street the route depends on must be walkable without scraping by a player who is paying attention.

avoid.said: What I meant by other "models" for movement was like that - completely different genre/styles of movements, not tied to our original "drunken" movement style
avoid.means: When asked for options, offer things that are different in kind, not the same thing with different numbers.

avoid.said: The tail should cause some damage, but not as much as it is
avoid.means: The tail must not be the main source of damage. On the course a careful run should lose fewer buildings to the tail than to the body.

avoid.said: actual slide (not just getting down slowly)
avoid.means: Posture changes the player asks for happen at once.

avoid.said: Movement felt a little lifeless. That is, kinda blocky. Strafing, turning didn't feel like I was actually turning
avoid.means: No body snaps to face a direction or slides sideways. A turn takes time, travels an arc that widens with speed, and leans; the head, chest and tail each arrive at their own moment. (test/runner.test.ts: 'turns on an arc that widens with speed, leaning into it'.)

The slide was starting; it looked the same as the crouch (same pose, legs still walking), so it read as nothing happening. A move must look and sound unlike every other pose from its first frame, and say what it is on the HUD.

avoid.said: Tail movement is off, it pretty much just spins around the character
avoid.means: Through any turn the tail stays behind the body: it may swing wide and lag by a fraction of a second, never come round the side. (test/runner.test.ts: 'keeps its tail behind it through a turn'.)

superseded.said: these settings are feeling a little better
superseded.then: playtest 6: "movement is OK, but not fun. It feels very sluggish." Those values are kept as the Lumbering style (key 1); they are no longer the default.
